newsitem.title: USA: Ice keeps Illinois, Mississippi river traffic slow.
newsitem.headline: Ice keeps Illinois, Mississippi river traffic slow.

text.p: Blowing winds and falling temperatures in the U.S. Midwest caused more icing Thursday that further hindered barge traffic on the Illinois and Mississippi Rivers, river officials said.
"We're moving pretty slow, but we're still moving," said Rick Kemp, assistant lockmaster at Lock 27 on the Mississippi River 10 miles north of St. Louis.

Snow and freezing rain fell in the area on Wednesday and created some icing problems. However, the river was expected to stay open as long as tows continued to move through the locks, Kemp said. On the Illinois River at Beardstown in central Illinois, river officials reported heavy winds had started to blow and ice was a problem for barges moving through the lock.
"Our lock is icing up, and there are places that they are having trouble getting through," a lock official said.
River traffic was still moving at that point on the Illinois, but as the weather grows colder, more and more problems were developing, the official said.
Grain merchandisers said transportation problems on the river will worsen if temperatures drop below zero as forecast.
"There's a little bit of movement in the lower half (of the Illinois river)," but it's only going to get worse as the temperature falls," a river dealer said.
An Army Corps of Engineers official in Le Clair, Iowa said that temperatures had already fallen below zero there, and ice cover on that stretch of the Mississippi was "tremendous."
An Arctic-like air mass is forecast to move south from Canada into the Midwest beginning Thursday.
Temperatures as of 1000 CST/1600 GMT were two degrees Fahrenheit in most of Illinois, and were several degrees below zero F in most of Iowa, according to data from Weather Express, in Omaha, Neb.
